blocks.heading: Whichever Path You Pick, Do Not Let

items.text: If you cannot pass all three within a reasonable early stretch, the plan needs a rebuild, not more time.
One finished, shippable piece of work in your chosen lane, a deployed website, three real design case studies, a paid client project, or a cleared government-exam tier.
ITI, CS, coding bootcamps, and government exam prep all demand serious, structured study, often for years.
Mukesh Ambani, Azim Premji, Ritesh Agarwal, and Nikhil Kamath dropped out and built massive companies, but this is survivorship bias in its purest form.
A skill with zero live job postings or client demand in your target city or remote market is a hobby, not a career plan yet.

blocks.heading: Without a Degree, No Company Will Even

items.text: "Just start a YouTube channel or become an influencer, degrees are outdated now."
"Everyone successful today dropped out of college."
"A degree is only a formality, it does not matter what you study."

blocks.heading: Graduate Unemployment in India Sits At Roughly

items.text: Only about 42.6% of Indian graduates are considered employable, according to the Mercer-Mettl India Graduate Skill Index, drawn from 2,700+ campuses and over a million students.
82% of Indian employers say they struggle to find candidates with the right practical skills, meaning real, unmet demand exists for people who can prove capability.

blocks.heading: Degree-Only Myth Vs the Degree-Optional Truth

items.text: Doesn't explain why 11.2% of graduates are unemployed and only 42.6% are considered employable by industry standards.
Ignores that 82% of employers say the real gap is practical skill, not credential count.
Treats every degree as equal, when employability swings from roughly 58% to 78% depending on the field.

blocks.heading: Name the Specific Path, Not Something

items.text: Bring the real cost and real timeline.
Show one piece of current evidence.
Name your own backup plan out loud.
